idiom_name: explicit if plus panic for broken invariants; error returns for expected failures
implementation_notes: Go deliberately has no assertions - the FAQ argues they become a crutch for skipping proper error handling - so every invariant check is written out: an if with a comparison, then panic for an internal state the program should never reach or an error return for anything a caller can supply. The idiomatic Must convention used by regexp.MustCompile and template.Must is appropriate for package initialization or constructors; request-facing methods should return errors.
pitfalls: panic is acceptable only for states the program should never reach; asserting on user input turns a recoverable error into a crashed server, which the FAQ warns about explicitly.
There is no debug/release switch, so every check is paid for in production: keep predicates cheap or move heavy ones into tests.
A stale predicate panics only when its code path finally runs, and no compiler pass evaluates it; keep the invariant checks covered by tests and reviewed like production logic.
